description: CAM-150 B-1 substrate: make the worker dev container correct, runnable, authenticated, firewalled, and preflight-wired (workers still spawn on host; B-2/CAM-152 flips the spawn).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed: --cap-add=NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW adds a single Linux capability (preferred over --privileged); -e VAR (name-only, no '=value') inherits the value from the invoking shell env and passes it to the container; -v name:/path mounts a named volume and -v /host:/ctr (or --mount type=bind) a bind mount; --user <name|uid>; -d --name for a long-lived detached named container; docker exec -it attaches a controlling TTY. No deprecations affecting these flags.

Confirmed --ipset=/<domain>[/<domain>...]/<setname>[,setname...] places the resolved IP addresses of queries for the listed domains (subdomain matching included, same as --address) into the named Netfilter ipset dynamically as DNS answers arrive. This is the mechanism that keeps CDN-backed allowlist hosts current across IP rotation over the container lifetime (vs the frozen dig-once ipset).

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [.devcontainer/init-firewall.sh:17]: US-004 allowlist drift: the declared ALLOWED_DOMAINS array (7 entries: ...,*.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com; NO raw.githubusercontent.com) has diverged from the actual dnsmasq --ipset directives (7 domain args: ...,github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, objects.githubusercontent.com; *.github.com folded into github.com, and raw ADDED). The array is now decorative (only feeds echo lines); the dnsmasq directives are the real egress source of truth. Net: the actual egress-reachable union is 8 hosts (adds raw.githubusercontent.com), not the 'exactly 7' the AC requires. US-004 note F-02 explicitly required the test to 'parse the resolved allow-set (ALLOWED_DOMAINS + any dnsmasq --ipset domain args) and assert host-set equality with the 7 required hosts (drop OR add fails)', but test/supervisor/worker-container-firewall.test.ts only parses ALLOWED_DOMAINS and never inspects the --ipset domain args, so dropping/adding a real dnsmasq directive would NOT fail the test. AC[1] also names raw.githubusercontent.com as one of the required 7 (array dropped it) and AC[2] requires the runbook table to stay accurate (docs/recovery-runbook.md now lists objects.githubusercontent.com but omits raw.githubusercontent.com, which is actually reachable). Fix: reconcile ALLOWED_DOMAINS == dnsmasq --ipset domains == runbook table == the test's REQUIRED_HOSTS as a single source of truth, and have the firewall test assert host-set equality against the parsed --ipset domain args (per F-02) so a dropped or added egress directive fails.

Preserve the exact 7-domain allowlist and the self-verify, and fix objects.github.com -> objects.githubusercontent.com.
acceptanceCriteria: init-firewall.sh uses dnsmasq --ipset=/<domain>.../allowed-domains matching (dynamic resolved-IP insertion) instead of the one-shot dig+ipset-add loop, so allowlisted CDN hosts survive IP rotation without a frozen-IP drop. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'dnsmasq' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]

The 7-domain allowlist semantics are preserved: a named test parses ALLOWED_DOMAINS from .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh and asserts the set of egress-reachable hosts equals EXACTLY the 7 required hosts (api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, github.com, *.github.com, registry.npmjs.org, raw.githubusercontent.com) so a DROPPED or ADDED domain fails; the count-of-7 comment/guard is intact. Host-set equivalence is asserted (a dnsmasq rewrite may fold github.com + *.github.com into one --ipset directive), NOT a literal directive/line count. [oracle: bun test]

The LFS subdomain is corrected: objects.github.com is replaced by objects.githubusercontent.com (objects.github.com is not a real LFS host). [oracle: grep -q 'objects.githubusercontent.com' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]
objects.github.com (the non-LFS host) no longer appears as a bare subdomain in the script. [oracle: ! grep -Eq 'objects\.github\.com([^u]|$)' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]

The self-verify step is preserved (allowed host api.anthropic.com must succeed; blocked host example.com must fail); the default-deny OUTPUT policy and DNS(53)/loopback/established rules remain. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'Self-verify' .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh]

The dnsmasq requirement is reflected in the Dockerfile install layer (dnsmasq is apt-installed alongside iptables/ipset/dnsutils/curl). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'dnsmasq' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]
